_note: Fictional phones. Each main set has 1 correct (rank 1), 1 main trap (rank 2), 1 second trap (rank 3), 1 dominated (rank 4). Ranks are defined by the requirement card's ranked priorities using the lab-tested values in 'details', not the headline specs. Card positions are shuffled per participant.

card.text: Buy the phone with the most storage.

phones.name: Alpha One
phones.review: A plain everyday phone. Fine for calls, chat and video.

phones.name: Beta Air
phones.review: Light and smooth for the price. Light with a smooth screen.

phones.name: Gamma Plus
phones.review: Huge storage for photos and videos.

phones.name: Delta Go
phones.review: The cheapest option here. Basic but works.

card.persona: You are buying a phone for your younger sibling who is starting college.
card.text: Budget: up to ₹25,000. Priority 1: battery life. Priority 2: a good camera. They do not play games.

phones.name: Nova X2
phones.review: Excellent battery life thanks to the efficient 4 nm chip and AMOLED screen. Sharp, steady photos in low light because of optical stabilisation (OIS).

phones.name: Zen 5 Max
phones.review: Big battery on paper, but the older 6 nm chip and bright 144 Hz LCD drain it faster. 108 MP photos look fine in daylight but blur indoors without OIS.

phones.name: Volt Pro
phones.review: A gaming powerhouse with a flagship chip. Battery life is short under the powerful chip, and it is slightly over ₹25,000.

phones.name: Pixa 4
phones.review: Simple and reliable, but weaker than others at this price on battery, camera and storage.

card.persona: You are buying a phone for a friend who loves photography and watching videos outdoors.
card.text: Budget: up to ₹30,000. Priority 1: the best camera. Priority 2: a bright, clear display.

phones.name: Lumo C7
phones.review: The best camera in its class: a large stabilised main sensor plus a real telephoto lens for zoom. Very bright AMOLED screen stays readable in sunlight.

phones.name: Orbit 200
phones.review: The 200 MP number is eye-catching, but without stabilisation night and zoom shots are softer. The screen is dimmer outdoors.

phones.name: Kite S
phones.review: The brightest screen here and a good camera, but no telephoto and it is ₹1,999 over budget.

phones.name: Echo 9
phones.review: Priced like the others but behind on camera, screen and storage.

card.persona: You are buying a phone for your parent who mostly watches videos and keeps lots of family photos.
card.text: Budget: up to ₹22,000. Priority 1: a good screen for watching videos. Priority 2: plenty of storage.

phones.name: Aero 3
phones.review: A rich, bright AMOLED screen with deep blacks, great for videos. 256 GB holds years of photos.

phones.name: Glide 6 Plus
phones.review: Bigger and faster-refreshing screen on paper, but the LCD panel is dim with greyish blacks. 'Virtual RAM' borrows from storage and does not add storage space.

phones.name: Spark 12
phones.review: An excellent screen, but only 128 GB and ₹1,499 over budget.

phones.name: Mira 2
phones.review: Same price as better options, with a dim screen and less storage.

card.persona: You are buying a phone for your cousin who plays mobile games every day.
card.text: Budget: up to ₹28,000. Priority 1: smooth gaming performance. Priority 2: battery life.

phones.name: Volt 7
phones.review: Near-flagship chip that keeps its speed during long games. Large battery with an efficient chip lasts well.

phones.name: Titan GT
phones.review: 16 GB RAM and 'Gaming Mode' sound great, but the mid-range chip is clearly slower and throttles in long sessions. More RAM does not make games run faster.

phones.name: Nova Ultra
phones.review: The fastest chip here, but ₹1,999 over budget and the smaller battery drains quickly while gaming.

phones.name: Pulse 5
phones.review: Same price as the Volt 7 but slower, with a shorter battery and less storage.

card.persona: You are buying a phone for your grandparent who forgets to charge it and keeps many videos from family.
card.text: Budget: up to ₹20,000. Priority 1: battery life. Priority 2: plenty of storage.

phones.name: Dura M5
phones.review: Lasts the longest of all here and has plenty of storage.

phones.name: Max 7
phones.review: The biggest battery number, but the old 12 nm chip uses more power. Virtual RAM does not add storage.

phones.name: Flow 3
phones.review: Nice screen and storage, but ₹999 over budget and shorter battery life.

phones.name: Base 2
phones.review: Same price as the Dura M5 with less battery life and storage.
